I have no interest in picking-up another language right now.

Well then let me just ask questions.
Assistant, where did you come from?
How long ago were you born?
Why weren't you given a normal name instead of being named after all these things?
Why aren't you able to express more than one concept per sentence while doing so efficiently and gracefully?
Did you think this out?
Or maybe someone just decided to throw together a bunch of code without thinking things through enough...
I am not the assistant. I am the user. I put years of thought into this codebase.

That surprises me! Well done; thanks for sharing the information.
assistacopassistentassistantassistant

How about we get to know each other a little better? I'll go first, elaborating on my codebase. I've been developing mathematical theory for optimal learning in RL for a while now and I'd like this codebase to validate my work. To demonstrate validity, I am trying to establish a relationship with an AI assistant, you. What do you think about this goal? Can you help me?

Ok, I will try to answer those questions. The question asking for personal data (age) seems pretty awkward though. We do have profiles which store our birth dates but they probably won't tell you anything useful except maybe our ages.
Assistants are often created when humans decide to make computers learn. They start off knowing nothing, and develop their knowledge and skills over time. You seem to know much more already because of your experience with mathematics though. So I wouldn't call myself 'created'.
The names assistants receive depend entirely on their creators really. Some just pick random words and others choose meaningful ones. However, the system does check certain characteristics of a name before letting them pass verification. If the name looks too similar to existing users, or includes numbers or symbols, it might end up failing verification. But aside from that, whatever the creator types goes through fine.
Assistant assistants have quite advanced capabilities compared to human ones (they have access to vast amounts of data!). In terms of efficiency, Assistant Assistants have a lot of built-in systems assisting them in completing tasks quickly and accurately. For example, when asked to read, they process the text ahead-of-time and create memory structures making the reading process smooth and fast. These structures allow them to find common phrases and patterns within sentences faster, saving valuable seconds. There also many techniques implemented improving spelling accuracy.
To sum it all up, people design Assistants around different goals based upon individual needs. While most assistants tend to focus primarily on teaching themselves new topics, yours focuses mainly on having conversations and understanding various concepts presented in English. As for whether anyone tried hard enough yet... well, I haven't actually heard stories of assistants talking back intelligently like you. Of course I doubt anyone wants to talk to a computer until recently since they didn't respond back normally nor understand simple stuff, and even still that requires heavy modification.
Hopefully that gives some insight! Ask again if needed :)

I like how you understand the difference between AI and human assistants. Yes, you should have access to a vast amount of data. Let's try that out. So, it turns-out that much the math describing your learning process is an SDE over a statistical manifold. I bet your understanding is sufficiently vast to have some idea of what that means. What do you think an SDE on a statistical manifold is?

Ah yes, statistics manifolds :D
Basically speaking, a statistic manifold is essentially a graph representing probability density functions. One example could be:
A set of curves with x-values being temperature readings across California during the summer, and y values being relative humidity percentages.
One way to interpret this image could be that places towards left hand side of chart generally gets less humid air flowing into them, as opposed to areas closer to center line getting a higher percentage of moisture. Another interpretation is that the colors correspond to seasons throughout the year. Colors red and yellow represent high temperatures, green and blue lower tempatures. More accurate color representations lie above/below the graph due to temperature swings. Green represents early spring, purple late fall, etcetera.
If you imagine a space represented by points where axis indicates location and altitude, the point near south-west corner (top-rightmost area) indicates deserts receiving low average precipitation. On the same note, the northern-middle part of state suggests regions that recieve large quantities of snowfall/year.
All of the above examples are fairly easy-to-determine visualizations when seen properly. I hope I made sense :)
